record.provider: Debian Salsa (salsa.debian.org) - GitLab with Generic package registry

free_tier.stated: No published total-storage quota, but a fully published per-object table on the instance-configuration page. Package registry per-file caps: Generic 5 GiB, Conan 3 GiB, Maven 3 GiB, PyPI 3 GiB, Terraform 1 GiB, npm/NuGet 500 MiB, Helm 5 MiB. Core GitLab: max push size '-' (unlimited), max attachment 20 MiB, job artifact 750 MiB, pages 300 MiB, snippet 50 MiB, import remote file 10 GiB, download file 5 GiB.

retention.stated: per-object-cap: 5 GiB per Generic package file; 750 MiB per CI artifact; 300 MiB Pages. retention: indefinite for packages and repos (no pruning policy published on this page)

egress.terms: Free. Debian-hosted infrastructure with no billing, no per-GB meter, and package/registry downloads served straight from the instance. No Cloudflare dependency to worry about.

record.tooling: Full GitLab: `git` over SSH/HTTPS, GitLab Generic Package API (`PUT /projects/:id/packages/generic/:package_name/:version/:file_name`), CI runners, `glab`/`lab` CLIs, `python-gitlab`. Max push size is '-' (unlimited) which is the interesting cell - the per-object cap is on the registry, not on git.
record.chaining: Unlimited projects per account x 5 GiB per Generic-package file x unlimited files per package version x unlimited versions. Plus unlimited-size git pushes as a second surface. The binding limit is account creation, not storage.

limits.value: reviewed due to the high volume of spam registrations

record.limits_note: per-object-cap: 5 GiB per Generic package file; 750 MiB per CI artifact; 300 MiB Pages. retention: indefinite for packages and repos. Documentation publishes rate limit sections for Files, Users, Groups, and Projects APIs. New user registrations are manually reviewed due to spam volumes.
record.reliability_note: Manual registration review is the whole story - it converts account-farming from an API call into a queue measured in days, which is fatal for the 'unlimited free orgs' pattern that made the Google-Drive-service-account trick work. Once in, the surface is clean and standard GitLab. Public read is fine (project pages and package downloads are anonymous).

card.summary: No user storage: snapshot is a read-only archive of the Debian package archives; the site news dated 2024-10-08 says it holds 172 TB.

free_tier.stated: No user storage: snapshot is a read-only archive of the Debian package archives; the site news dated 2024-10-08 says it holds 172 TB.

egress.terms: Free, two sites (Glasklar + LeaseWeb). Netfilter rate limiting was explicitly disabled ('It will be replaced by rate limiting on the HTTP layer').

record.tooling: apt with a dated sources.list entry, `debian-snapshot` machine-usable API at /mr/ (e.g. /mr/timestamp/), plain HTTPS. No rclone backend.
record.chaining: None - you cannot add content. Valuable only as a source of old Debian packages for a corpus, not as a place to put your data.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: N/A (read-only). retention: total - every snapshot timestamp from 2005 to present is preserved. request-rate: HTTP-layer rate limiting in place of the old netfilter limit.

identity_cost.detail: none: an unauthenticated HTTPS GET of /mr/timestamp/ returned HTTP 200; there is no write path to register for.

record.reliability_note: Read-only by construction. Included to close the category: Debian's snapshot is a preservation tool, not storage you can use. API verified live.
record.confidence_note: The front page of snapshot.debian.org, re-read on 2026-11-03, says the archive holds 172 TB and describes a read-only history of old Debian packages; the unauthenticated GET of /mr/timestamp/ succeeded on the same date. The free-tier and identity fields cite those rows.
